messages.subject: Vectorization
parts:
Hi everyone,

I have the attached code, which is written using the multivariate normal distribution; I would like to convert the code to be in univariate normal distribution using vectorization; in the multivariate normal distribution, the precision matrix is a diagonal matrix.

The code using multivariate normal:
N <- 64
S <- 64

mybeta <- c(2, 0, 0, 4, 8)
set.seed(1)
x1 <- rnorm(64);
x2 <- rnorm(64);
x3 <- rnorm(64);
x4 <- rnorm(64);
x5 <- rnorm(64);
y  <- cbind(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5) %*% mybeta + rnorm(64)
## replicate y 64 times to make a square matrix for easy implementation
y <- matrix(y, nrow = length(y), ncol = length(y), byrow = FALSE)

library(nimble)

Code <- nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:S) {
    y[1:N, i] ~ dmnorm(mu[1:N, i],  tau[1:N, 1:N, i])
    mu[1:N, i] <- b[i, 1] * x1[1:N] + b[i, 2] * x2[1:N] + b[i, 3] *
      x3[1:N] + b[i, 4] * x4[1:N] + b[i, 5] * x5[1:N]
    tau[1:N, 1:N, i] <- diag(psi[i] * exp(-Dist[1:N, i]/lambda))
    for (j in 1:5) {
      b[i, j] ~ dnorm(0, tau = tau_b[ind[j] + 1])
      ind[j] ~ dbern(gamma[j])
      tau_b[1] <- tau_b0
      tau_b[2] <- tau_b0 * c
      gamma[j] ~ dbeta(0.5, 0.5)
    }
    b0[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    psi[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
  }
  lambda ~ dunif(0, D)
})

netdist <- read.csv('country_dist.csv')
my_points <- matrix(c(netdist$Longitude,    # Create longitude/latitude matrix
                      netdist$Latitude),ncol=2)

colnames(my_points) <- c("longitude", "latitude")

my_points


library(rdist)

df <- my_points
# distance matrices
dist_mat <- pdist(df)
dist_1 <- pdist(df[, 1])
dist_2 <- pdist(df[, 2])
# product distance matrix
dist_prod <- product_metric(dist_1, dist_2)


netdist<- (dist_prod )
dist2 <- (netdist)

Data <- list(y = y, x1 = x1, x2 = x2, x3 = x3, x4 = x4, x5 = x5,
                Dist = dist2)

Const <- list(S = S, N = N, D = 50, tau_b0 = 100, c = 0.0001)

Inits <- list(psi = rep(1, Const$S), ind = c(1, 1, 0, 0, 0),
                 gamma = rep(0.5, 5), lambda = 10)

mcmc.out <- nimbleMCMC(code =Code, data = Data, constants = Const,
                       inits = Inits, thin = 1, niter = 5000, nchains = 1, nburnin = 2000,
                       monitors = c("b", "psi", "lambda"), setSeed = TRUE)



library(coda)
pos_mcmc <- as.mcmc(mcmc.out)
par(mar=c(1,1,1,1))

plot(pos_mcmc[,1:5])


#######The univariate normal distribution

N <- 64
S <- 64

mybeta <- c(2, 0, 0, 4, 8)
set.seed(1)
x1 <- rnorm(64);
x2 <- rnorm(64);
x3 <- rnorm(64);
x4 <- rnorm(64);
x5 <- rnorm(64);
y  <- cbind(x1, x2, x3, x4, x5) %*% mybeta + rnorm(64)
y <- as.vector(y)
library(nimble)
dnorm_vec2 <- nimbleFunction( ## Define the distribution
  run = function(x = double(1), mean = double(1), sd = double(1), log = integer(0, default = 0)) {
    returnType(double(0))
    logProb <- sum(dnorm(x, mean, sd, log = TRUE))
    if(log) return(logProb)
    else return(exp(logProb))
  })
registerDistributions('dnorm_vec2')


Code <- nimbleCode({
  for (i in 1:S) {
    y[1:N] ~  dnorm_vec2(linpred[1:N,i], sigma[1:N,i])
    linpred[1:N,i] <-b[i, 1] * x1[1:N] + b[i, 2] * x2[1:N] + b[i, 3] * x3[1:N]+ b[i, 4] * x4[1:N]+ b[i, 5] * x5[1:N]
    tau[1:N,i] <- psi[i] * exp(-Dist[1:N, i]/lambda)
   
    sigma[1:N,i] <- 1/ tau[1:N,i]
    for (j in 1:5) {
      b[i, j] ~ dnorm(0, tau = tau_b[ind[j] + 1])
      ind[j] ~ dbern(gamma[j])
      tau_b[1] <- tau_b0
      tau_b[2] <- tau_b0 * c
      gamma[j] ~ dbeta(0.5, 0.5)
    }
    b0[i] ~ dnorm(0, 1)
    psi[i] ~ dgamma(1, 1)
  }
  lambda ~ dunif(0, D)
})

netdist <- read.csv('country_dist.csv')
my_points <- matrix(c(netdist$Longitude,    # Create longitude/latitude matrix
                      netdist$Latitude),ncol=2)

colnames(my_points) <- c("longitude", "latitude")

my_points

# dist_mat <- pdist(my_points)


df <- my_points
# distance matrices
dist_mat <- pdist(df)
dist_1 <- pdist(df[, 1])
dist_2 <- pdist(df[, 2])
# product distance matrix
dist_prod <- product_metric(dist_1, dist_2)



netdist<- (dist_prod )
dist2 <- (netdist)

Data <- list(y = y, x1 = x1, x2 = x2, x3 = x3, x4 = x4, x5 = x5,
                Dist = dist2)

Const <- list(S = S, N = N, D = 50, tau_b0 = 100, c = 0.0001)

Inits <- list(psi_y = rep(1,Const$S), ind = c(1, 1, 0, 0, 0),
                 gamma = rep(0.5, 5), lambda = 10)

mcmc.out2 <- nimbleMCMC(code = Code, data = Data, constants = Const,
                        inits = Inits, thin = 1, niter = 5000, nchains = 1, nburnin = 2000,
                        monitors = c("b", "psi", "lambda"), setSeed = TRUE)

library(coda)
pos_mcmc2 <- as.mcmc(mcmc.out2)

## plot the first five parameter estimates
plot(pos_mcmc2[,1:5])

messages.subject: Re: Vectorization
parts:
Hi Suzy,

I am not sure why you replicate your vector y into a matrix and then use each column each time in a for loop. Given you are considering a multivariate normal distribution, this is not needed. In your code, you repeated declaring some nodes, like those inside the j loop within the i loop. This does not make sense in BUGS language. In addition, the way you specified the precision matrix for mnorm is not correct. The matrix you generated was not diagonal. Another issue is that the default parameter in dnorm is prec instead of sd. In your custom dnorm_vec2 function you intended to use sd but inside the code it's actually prec. I have fixed all these. In the code attached you will see the two methods match well. Please let me know if you have any questions. 

Best wishes,
Wei

Hi Wei,

Thank you for getting back to me.

The multivariate code is provided by the authors of the paper titled "Geographically Weighted Regression Analysis for Spatial Economics Data: a Bayesian Recourse."  which can be seen here https://ys-xue.github.io/Bayesian-GWR/
using the code provided by the authors for extensive data set is computationally expensive, so I am thinking of a way to convert the code to be in univaraite normal distributions.


In this algorithm, we are interested in finding the posterior for each parameter for each region i. The authors used y[1:N, i] ~ dmnorm(mu_y[1:N, i], prec = tau_y0[1:N, 1:N, i]) where the precision matrix is a diagonal matrix.


In my suggested algorithm I used dnorm_vec2 , I got the posterior for each parameter in each region, but the results from both models are too different. 



I was also thinking maybe the issue is related to the vectorizations, where the vectorized one might need to run for more iterations to converge because the mvnormal approach might be blocking some of the parameters by default (the vectorized function wouldn't block by default). So I ran the suggested algorithm for more iterations, but it does not work.
Could you please advise in this regard?

Hi Suzy,

I am not sure why you replicate your vector y into a matrix and then use each column each time in a for loop. Given you are considering a multivariate normal distribution, this is not needed. In your code, you repeated declaring some nodes, like those inside the j loop within the i loop. This does not make sense in BUGS language. In addition, the way you specified the precision matrix for mnorm is not correct. The matrix you generated was not diagonal. Another issue is that the default parameter in dnorm is prec instead of sd. In your custom dnorm_vec2 function you intended to use sd but inside the code it's actually prec. I have fixed all these. In the code attached you will see the two methods match well. Please let me know if you have any questions.
